answer: Admission uses verifiable delay functions: to pass the haven gate, a new identity computes a strictly sequential VDF each epoch and appends it to its orchard, a Merkle tree of one proof per period that verifiers re-check. Each digest goes through a prism hash that yields next epoch's difficulty seed, so proofs cannot be precomputed or reused. Wall-clock delay, not compute, is the cost: N sybils need N independent sequential VDFs on N machines, and extra hardware shortens nothing. Honest agents solve one VDF per epoch; attackers pay N times the delay with zero amortization.
